text:
Ash Wilson: Heads up — customer (acme-saas) reporting lots of streaming sessions being marked as 5xx. They say client disconnects mid-stream but logs show write errors and proxy FINs. Billing flagged it as gateway 5xx.

Maria Chen: Can you paste a short trace + sample client request?

Ash Wilson: Pastes minimal repro.
```
POST /v1/responses/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "open-llama-7b-stream",
  "input": "streaming test",
  "max_tokens": 500
}

Client side: node fetch streaming and client closes connection after ~1.2s (simulated flaky network)
Server logs (excerpt):
[2026-03-15T12:34:11Z] gateway: conn=abcd1234 upstream_write_error: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.1.2.3:52344: write: broken pipe
[2026-03-15T12:34:11Z] proxy: halfclose detected, upstream state=FIN_WAIT
[2026-03-15T12:34:11Z] classifier: request_label=5xx (gateway.error)
```

Ash Wilson: Customer insists this should be classified as client disconnect and not counted for 5xx billing. They have a video of the client aborting.

Kevin Patel: Thanks, adding notes. Two quick asks: 1) exact request id/trace id? 2) do we have an ingress span showing client FIN vs upstream RST?

Ash Wilson: trace_id=trace-0x9f7a. In the full trace the ingress shows `read: connection reset by peer` then our gateway attempts write and gets `broken pipe`.

Simon Ortega: This is a classic race: client closes (FIN) then server writes and hits EPIPE. Our metrics pipeline currently marks the write error as gateway 5xx because upstream write failed. That aligns with past disputes.

Maria Chen: Do we have the classification heuristic code snippet? I remember we decide based on socket error type and timing window. If client-close within X ms of last write, we mark as client_abort. Otherwise 5xx.

Simon Ortega: Right — code gist: `if (socket.closed && time_since_last_client_byte < 200ms) label = CLIENT_ABORT; else label = GATEWAY_ERROR;`

Support Bot: FYI I'm attaching the billing tag: invoice-2026-03-account-9876 flagged for 12 events.

Kevin Patel: Customer asks for both a fix and an immediate mitigation (don't bill these until we validate). Suggestion: add a temporary rule: if trace has client FIN or ECONNRESET before upstream error and total tokens returned < threshold, mark as client_abort and don't bill.

Maria Chen: Agreed. Quick mitigation steps: 1) create incident ticket and pause billing for the customer for a week; 2) adjust classification to prefer ingress-side close when present; 3) instrument a metric to surface write-after-close races.

Ash Wilson: I'll open the billing hold with ops.

Simon Ortega: For longer term we should: - expand the heuristic window to 1s for streaming responses - treat EPIPE following an ingress FIN as client disconnect (unless upstream returned 5xx body before FIN) - add a small trace flag `client_abort_hint` that services can set when they detect local client halfclose.

Kevin Patel: Can someone paste a minimal repro script we can run to generate identical logs? I'd like an automated test in our e2e suite.

Maria Chen: Quick node repro (simulate flaky client):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses/stream', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-test' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'open-llama-7b-stream', input: 'x'.repeat(1000), max_tokens: 500 })
  });
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  // read a chunk then abruptly close socket
  await reader.read();
  // simulate abrupt client close by closing underlying socket -> in node you can destroy the request 
  res.body.cancel();
})();
```

Simon Ortega: Nice. That will reproduce client-side abort and generate a write: broken pipe on the server if it tries to write after cancel.

Ash Wilson: Ops ticket: INC-2026-1789 opened, billing hold requested. Customer ok with temporary hold.

Kevin Patel: For the classifier change — Simon, can you open a PR to: 1) prefer ingress FIN within 1s; 2) add `client_abort_hint` annotation to traces; 3) add unit tests for the node repro. Tag me for review.

Simon Ortega: Will do, aim for Friday EOD.

Maria Chen: Also add a Grafana panel: `streaming.write_after_close.rate` and alert when > 0.1% of streams.

Support Bot: Billing hold confirmed for invoice-2026-03-account-9876.

Ash Wilson: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated with customer status and any follow-ups from engineering.

Simon Ortega: One more note — we should avoid automatically downgrading true upstream 5xx that happen before client FIN. If the upstream already returned a 502 payload (even small) and then client closes, that's still a server error. Heuristic must check for a successful write of an error body before classifying.

Kevin Patel: Good point. Add that check to the PR.

Maria Chen: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees repeat hits for this customer after the mitigation, ping the thread. :white_check_mark:
